evidence.title: Nonexistent package recommendations created a potential dependency pathway
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: Lanyado reports recurring nonexistent package recommendations and downloads of an empty package registered during the study.

source_locations.SRC-145: How — Research Process; Cross models hallucinations; Hallucinated Package Case Study; registerability qualifications; https://www.lasso.security/blog/ai-package-hallucinations

evidence.limitations: Downloads do not establish each downloader’s route or malicious execution. Some names could not be registered. Model selection, prompts and registry conditions constrain transfer; ambiguous denominators preclude adopting comparative rates here.
evidence.open_questions: Transfer beyond the described models, tasks and setting remains unestablished. Calendar observation dates not reported precisely are not inferred.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: Illustrates how recommendations can affect dependencies outside the model. The report does not establish that every download resulted from AI advice or caused compromise.
evidence.dispute_status: Source-attributed result; no systematic dispute or retraction clearance claimed.
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: AI-enabled capability
terms.definition: An organizational function delivered through an AI model and the people, tools, data, workflows, and dependencies required to produce its intended outcome. The capability—not only the model—is the relevant unit when discussing operational consequences.

terms.name: Reference environment integrity
terms.definition: The reliability, provenance, completeness, and resistance to manipulation of information used to make operational or assurance judgments, including documents, logs, telemetry, evidence, and monitoring outputs.
